newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand names winners for second stage power bid.
newsitem.headline: Thailand names winners for second stage power bid.

text.p: State-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) said on Monday two consortia have won contracts to sell EGAT up to 2,100 megawatts of power under the second stage of its independent power producer (IPP) scheme.
EGAT said in a statement it intended to buy up to 2,100 megawatts of power from the two consortia under 25-year contracts starting in the year 2001.
A consortium led by Tomen Corp of Japan won one contract to sell 1,400 megawatts power to EGAT. The other partners in the group include Imatran Voima Oy of Finland and Union Energy of Thailand.
The group's power plant, worth about 33 billion baht, will be located in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 300 km west of Bangkok, the agency said.
Under the other contract, EGAT will buy up to 700 megawatts of electricity from Gulf Power Generation Co Ltd, whose 22 billion baht power plant will be also located in Prachuap Khiri Khan.
Gulf Power Generation is a joint venture company between Gulf Electric Co Ltd and United States's Edison Mission Energy.
The consortia were the top bidders in EGAT's short list for the second stage of the IPP scheme, the agency said.
Under the two-stage IPP programme, EGAT plans to purchase a total of about 4,180 megawatts electricity by 2002 from private companies which will build, operate and own power plants.
EGAT will buy up to a total of 2,800 megawatts from private producers.
The utility is still negotiating with other bidders on the short list for the remaining 700 megawatts of electricity to be purchased in the second stage, it said.
